item.title: Building a 3D graphics engine in C++ from first-principles
item.description: Introduction Over the past few months I’ve been working on a 3D graphics engine from scratch in C++. In December, I came across donut.c (an ASCII rendering of a spinning donut) and wanted to learn how it worked so I implemented it in Python and then in C++. This is how it works: Create a circle of points and rotate the circle around a point to create a donut in 3D space Rotate the donut by applying rotation matrices to the points Use projection maths to create a z-buffer Use the dot product to calculate lighting And then you have a spinning donut in ASCII.
